exercises.heading: 2.8. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1–2 Use the given graph to estimate the value of each derivative. Then sketch the graph of $$f^{\prime}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Match the graph of each function in (a), (b), (c), and (d) with the graph of its derivative in (I), (II), (III), and (IV). Give reasons for your choices.

list.item: a. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, crosses the negative x axis, concave up, reaches a low point in the third quadrant, goes up and to the right through the origin, enters into the first quadrant, now concaves down, reaches a high point, goes down and to the right, crosses the positive x axis, and extends into the fourth quadrant.

b. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the third quadrant, rises linearly to the right by crossing the negative x axis, reaches its sharp high point in the second quadrant, falls linearly to the right through the origin, reaches its sharp low point in the fourth quadrant, then rises linearly to the right, crosses the positive x axis, and extends into the first quadrant.

c. Details An inverted bell-shaped curve, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the third quadrant very close to the x axis, goes down and to the right, initially concave down as it veers away from the x axis, then becoming concave up, reaches its low point on the negative y axis, enters into the fourth quadrant, mirroring its earlier path, veering toward the positive x axis while approaching it, and exits very close to and below the x axis.

d. Details An M-shaped curve, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the third quadrant from the bottom, goes up and to the right, concave down, crosses the negative x axis, reaches a high point in the second quadrant, goes gradually down and to the right, now concave up, and reaches its low point at the origin. It then enters into the first quadrant, becoming concave down again, reaches a high point, then goes steeply down and to the right, crosses the positive x axis, extends into the fourth quadrant, thus mirroring its earlier path.

I. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the third quadrant very close to the x axis, goes down and to the right, veering away from the x axis, concave up, reaches a low point in the third quadrant, then goes up and to the right through the origin. It then enters into the first quadrant, now concave down, reaches a high point, then goes down and to the right, veering toward the x axis, and exits the viewing window very close to and above the x axis. II. Details A downward opening parabola, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The parabola enters the third quadrant, goes up and to the right, crosses the negative x axis, reaches its vertex on the positive y axis, then goes down and to the right in the first quadrant, crosses the positive x axis, and extends into the fourth quadrant. III. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, crosses the negative x axis, concaves up, reaches its low point in the third quadrant, and then goes up and to the right through the origin. After the curve enters into the first quadrant, the curve becomes concave down, reaches its high point, goes down and to the right, crosses the positive x axis, and extends into the fourth quadrant. IV. Details A function with disconnected parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first part enters the second quadrant, runs horizontally rightward, and ends with an open dot near the y axis. The second part begins with an open dot in the third quadrant, directly below the open dot of the first part, runs horizontally rightward, crosses the negative y axis, and ends in the fourth quadrant with an open dot. The third part begins with an open dot in the first quadrant, directly above the open dot of the second part and directly across the open dot of the first part, and then runs horizontally rightward.

exercises.instruction: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 Trace or copy the graph of the given function $$f$$ . (Assume that the axes have equal scales.) Then use the method of Example 1 to sketch the graph of $$f^{\prime}$$ below it.

problem.paragraph: 4. Details An inverted bell-shaped curve, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, initially concave down, crosses the negative x axis, then becomes concave up, and reaches its low point on the negative y axis. It then goes up and to the right into the fourth quadrant, crosses the positive x axis, then becomes concave down, and exits the viewing window above the x axis, thus mirroring its earlier path.

5. Details A curve, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant above the x axis, goes down and to the right, concave up, crosses the negative x axis, reaches its low point in the third quadrant, goes steeply upward to the right by crossing the negative x axis, concave down, and reaches its high point on the positive y axis. It then goes down and to the right by crossing the positive x axis, concave up, again reaches its low point in the fourth quadrant, then goes gradually upward to the right, crosses the positive x axis, and exits the viewing window in the first quadrant above the x axis.

6. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant very close to the x axis, goes up and to the right, veering away from it, concave down, reaches its high point in the second quadrant, and then goes down and to the right through the origin. After it enters into the fourth quadrant, the curve then becomes concave up, reaches its low point, goes up and to the right, and veers toward the positive x axis, exiting the fourth quadrant very close to and below the x axis.

7. Details A curve, which is symmetric about the y axis, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve resembles the upper half of the circle. It begins on the negative x axis, goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches its high point on the positive y axis, then goes down and to the right, and ends on the positive x axis.

8. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the third quadrant below the negative x axis, goes up and to the right, concave up, crosses the negative x axis, and briefly levels out a certain point in the second quadrant. It then goes up and to the right, crosses the positive y axis, concave down, reaches its high point in the first quadrant, and then goes down and to the right, veering toward the positive x axis.

9. Details A curve with two parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first part enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, crosses the negative x axis, concave up, and reaches its low point in the third quadrant, then goes up and to the right through the fourth quadrant into the first quadrant until a certain point. From this point, the second part goes linearly downward to the right in the fourth quadrant by crossing the positive x axis.

10. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant, goes linearly down and to the right by crossing the negative axis, reaches its sharp low point in the third quadrant, then goes linearly up and to the right by crossing the negative x axis again, enters into the second quadrant, and runs horizontally rightward until a certain point near the y axis. The curve then goes linearly downward to the right through the origin, reaches its sharp low point, again goes linearly upward to the right by crossing the positive x axis, then runs horizontally rightward, and again falls linearly to the right into the fourth quadrant.

11. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, concave down, crosses the positive y axis, falls almost vertically downward in the first quadrant, now becoming concave up, veers toward the positive x axis, and exits very close to and above the x axis.

Shown is the graph of the population function $$P(t)$$ for yeast cells in a laboratory culture. Use the method of Example 1 to graph the derivative $$P^{\prime}(t)$$ . What does the graph of $$P^{\prime}$$ tell us about the yeast population?

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t (hours) and is displayed from 0 to 15 in increments of 5 units. The vertical axis is labeled P (yeast cells) and is displayed from 0 to 700 in increments of 100 units. The curve begins at approximately (0, 25) on the vertical axis, goes up and to the right, concave up, passes through the approximate point (7.5, 450), becoming concave down, and approaches the P-value of 700 as the curve proceeds rightward.

problem.paragraph: A rechargeable battery is plugged into a charger. The graph shows $$C(t)$$ , the percentage of full capacity that the battery reaches as a function of time $$t$$ elapsed (in hours).

list.item: What is the meaning of the derivative $$C^{\prime}(t)$$ ?

Sketch the graph of $$C^{\prime}(t)$$ . What does the graph tell you? Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t (hours) and is displayed from 0 to 12 in increments of 2 hours. The vertical axis C is labeled Percentage of full charge and is displayed from 0 to 100 in increments of 20 units. The curve begins at the origin, goes up and to the right through the approximate points (2, 53), (4, 80), and (6, 90), concave down, and approaches the C value of 100 as the curve proceeds rightward.

solution.paragraph: The instantaneous rate of change of percentage of full capacity with respect to elapsed time in hours
The rate of change of percentage of full capacity is decreasing and approaching $$0$$ .

problem.paragraph: The graph (from the US Department of Energy) shows how driving speed affects gas mileage. Fuel economy $$F$$ is measured in miles per gallon and speed $$\upsilon$$ is measured in miles per hour.

list.item: What is the meaning of the derivative $$F^{\prime}(\upsilon)$$ ?
Sketch the graph of $$F^{\prime}(\upsilon)$$ .

At what speed should you drive if you want to save on gas? Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis labeled v (miles per hour) is displayed from 0 to 70 in increments of 5 units. The vertical axis labeled F (miles per gallon) is displayed from 0 to 30 in increments of 10 units. The curve begins at the approximate point (5, 11), goes up and to the right through the approximate points (10, 18) and (20, 25), concave down, reaches a high point at approximately (50, 30), then goes down and to the right, and ends at the approximate point (80, 23).

problem.paragraph: The graph shows how the average surface water temperature $$f$$ of Lake Michigan varies over the course of a year (where $$t$$ is measured in months with $$t = 0$$ corresponding to January 1). The average was calculated from data obtained over a $$20$$ -year period ending in 2011. Sketch the graph of the derivative function $$f^{\prime}$$ . When is $$f^{\prime}(t)$$ largest?

The vertical axis labeled f (in degrees Fahrenheit) is displayed from 30 to 70 in increments of 10 units. Two short slanted segments on the vertical axis above the origin indicate that the viewing window has been compressed between f = 0 and f = 30. problem.paragraph: $$f(x) = \sin x$$

list.item: Estimate the values of $$f^{\prime}(0)$$ , $$f^{\prime}\left( \frac{1}{2} \right)$$ , $$f^{\prime}(1)$$ , and $$f^{\prime}(2)$$ by zooming in on the graph of $$f$$ .

Use symmetry to deduce the values of $$f^{\prime}\left( {- \frac{1}{2}} \right)$$ , $$f^{\prime}\left( {- 1} \right)$$ , $$f^{\prime}\left( {- 2} \right)$$ , and $$f^{\prime}\left( {- 3} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: The table gives the number $$N(t)$$ , measured in thousands, of minimally invasive cosmetic surgery procedures performed in the United States for various years $$t$$ .

list.item: What is the meaning of $$N^{\prime}(t)$$ ? What are its units?
Construct a table of estimated values for $$N^{\prime}(t)$$ .
Graph $$N$$ and $$N^{\prime}$$ .
How would it be possible to get more accurate values for $$N^{\prime}(t)$$ ?

problem.paragraph: The table gives the height as time passes of a typical pine tree grown for lumber at a managed site.
If $$H(t)$$ is the height of the tree after $$t$$ years, construct a table of estimated values for $$H^{\prime}$$ and sketch its graph.
Water temperature affects the growth rate of brook trout. The table shows the amount of weight gained by brook trout after $$24$$ days in various water temperatures.
If $$W(x)$$ is the weight gain at temperature $$x$$ , construct a table of estimated values for $$W^{\prime}$$ and sketch its graph. What are the units for $$W^{\prime}(x)$$ ?

Source: Adapted from J. Chadwick Jr., “Temperature Effects on Growth and Stress Physiology of Brook Trout: Implications for Climate Change Impacts on an Iconic Cold-Water Fish.” Masters Theses. Paper 897. 2012. scholarworks.umass.edu/theses/897.
Let $$P$$ represent the percentage of a city’s electrical power that is produced by solar panels $$t$$ years after January 1, 2020.

list.item: What does $$dP \slash dt$$ represent in this context?
Interpret the statement $$\left. \frac{dP}{dt} \right|_{t = 2} = 3.5$$

solution.paragraph: The rate at which the percentage of electrical power produced by solar panels is changing, in percentage points per year.
On January 1, 2022, the percentage of electrical power produced by solar panels was increasing at a rate of $$3.5$$ percentage points per year.

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$N$$ is the number of people in the United States who travel by car to another state for a vacation in a year when the average price of gasoline is $$p$$ dollars per gallon. Do you expect $$dN \slash dp$$ to be positive or negative? Explain.

exercises.instruction: 41, 42, 43, and 44 The graph of $$f$$ is given. State, with reasons, the numbers at which $$f$$ is not differentiable.

problem.paragraph: 41. Details A function with two parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 4 to 3 in increments of 1 unit. The first part begins at (negative 5, 0), goes linearly upward to the right in the second quadrant until x = negative 4, then goes down and to the right through the approximate point (negative 3.2, 0), concave up, and ends on the negative y axis with a solid dot. The second part begins with an open dot on the positive y axis, goes down and to the right, concave down, crosses the x axis at approximately (2.4, 0), extends into the fourth quadrant, now concave up. $$- 4({corner})$$ ; $$0({discontinuity})$$

42. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 2 to 4 in increments of 1 unit. The curve enters the second quadrant above the x axis, goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches its high point at x = negative 1.6, goes down and to the right, crosses the negative x axis at (negative 0.5, 0), then crosses the negative y axis, concave up, and reaches its low point in the fourth quadrant at x = 0.6, and then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant until x = 2. It then goes down and to the right, concave up, crosses the x axis at approximately (2.4, 0), and exits the fourth quadrant. There is an open dot on the curve at x = negative 1. Also, there is a solid dot directly above the open dot at x = negative 1.

43. Details A function with two parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from 0 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The first part of the function enters the third quadrant, goes up and to the right through the fourth quadrant, concave up, crosses the positive x axis at approximately (0.5, 0), and approaches x = 1 at the top as it further rises in the first quadrant. The second part enters the first quadrant at the top, very close to the right of x = 1, goes down and to the right, concave up, crosses the x axis at approximately (1.8, 0), reaches its low point at approximately x = 3.5 in the fourth quadrant, then rises steeply to the right, crosses the x axis at approximately (4.8, 0), then concave down, and exits the viewing window in the first quadrant at x = 7. $$1({not defined})$$ ; $$5({vertical tangent})$$

44. Details A function with two discontinuous parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 3 to 4 in increments of 1 unit. The first part enters the second quadrant from the left and runs horizontally rightward until x = negative 2, then goes up and to the right, concave down, crosses the positive y axis, and ends in the first quadrant with an open dot at x = 1. There is a solid dot directly below the open dot at x = 1. Directly below this solid dot, the second part of the function begins with an open dot at x = 1 in the first quadrant, goes down and to the right, concave down, crosses the x axis at approximately (2.3, 0), continues falling in the fourth quadrant until x = 3, then runs horizontally rightward in the fourth quadrant.

exercises.instruction: 47–48 The graphs of a function $$f$$ and its derivative $$f^{\prime}$$ are shown. Which is bigger, $$f^{\prime}\left( {- 1} \right)$$ or $$f^{''}(1)$$ ?

problem.paragraph: 47. Details Two curves are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 2 to 2 in increments of 1 unit. The first curve is symmetric about the y axis. It enters the viewing window in the second quadrant, goes down and to the right, concave up, crosses the negative x axis at approximately (negative 1.3, 0), reaches its low point in the third quadrant at x = negative 1, goes up and to the right, crosses the positive axis at approximately (negative 0.5, 0), concave down, and reaches its high point on the positive y axis. It then goes down and to the right, crosses the positive x axis at approximately (0.5, 0), concave up, reaches its low point in the fourth quadrant at x = 1, then goes up and to the right in the first quadrant by crossing the x axis at approximately (1.3, 0). The second curve enters the third quadrant, goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches its high point, then goes down and to the right by intersecting the first curve at two different points, concave up, and reaches its low point at approximately x = negative 0.5. It then goes up and to the right, crosses the negative y axis, again reaches its high point in the fourth quadrant at approximately x = 0.5, then falls to a low point by intersecting the first curve at two different points, again goes up and to the right in the first quadrant. $$f^{''}(1)$$

48. Details Two curves are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 2 to 2 in increments of 1 unit. The first curve enters with a low point in the third quadrant at x = negative 2, goes up and to the right by crossing the negative x axis at (negative 1.5, 0), then rises to a high point at approximately x = negative 0.7, goes down and to the right through the third quadrant, concave up, and reaches its low point in the fourth quadrant at approximately x = 0.4. It then goes up and to the right, crosses the positive x axis at (1, 0), concave down, reaches its high point at approximately x = 1.8, and then goes down and to the right in the fourth quadrant. The second curve enters the third quadrant from the left below the x axis, goes up and to the right, crosses the x axis at (negative 2, 0), concave down, reaches its high point at approximately x = negative 1.5, goes down and to the right by intersecting the first curve at x = negative 1, crosses the negative x axis at approximately (negative 0.7, 0), concave up, and reaches its low point in the third quadrant at approximately x = negative 0.2. It then goes up and to the right by intersecting the first curve, crosses the positive x axis at approximately (0.4, 0), concave down, reaches its high point at x = 1, then goes down and to the right in the fourth quadrant by crossing the x axis at approximately (1.8, 0).

problem.paragraph: The figure shows graphs of $$f$$ , $$f^{\prime}$$ , $$f^{''}$$ , and $$f^{'''}$$ . Identify each curve, and explain your choices.

image.alt: Details Four curves are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first curve labeled a, is an upward opening parabola that is symmetric about the y axis. problem.paragraph: Derivatives of Even and Odd Functions Recall that a function $$f$$ is called even if $$f( - x) = f(x)$$ for all $$x$$ in its domain and odd if $$f( - x) = - f(x)$$ for all such $$x$$ . Prove each of the following.

exercises.instruction: 64–65 Left- and Right-Hand Derivatives The left-hand and right-hand derivatives of $$f$$ at $$a$$ are defined by $$f_{-}^{\prime}(a) = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0^{-}}\frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$$ and $$f_{+}^{\prime}(a) = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0^{+}}\frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$$ if these limits exist. Then $$f^{\prime}(a)$$ exists if and only if these one sided derivatives exist and are equal.

problem.paragraph: Find $$f_{-}^{\prime}(0)$$ and $$f_{+}^{\prime}(0)$$ for the given function $$f$$ . Is $$f$$ differentiable at $$0$$ ?

exercises.paragraph: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was born in Leipzig in 1646 and studied law, theology, philosophy, and mathematics at the university there, graduating with a bachelor’s degree at age 17. After earning his doctorate in law at age 20, Leibniz entered the diplomatic service and spent most of his life traveling to the capitals of Europe on political missions. In particular, he worked to avert a French military threat against Germany and attempted to reconcile the Catholic and Protestant churches.

His serious study of mathematics did not begin until 1672 while he was on a diplomatic mission in Paris. There he built a calculating machine and met scientists, like Huygens, who directed his attention to the latest developments in mathematics and science. Leibniz sought to develop a symbolic logic and system of notation that would simplify logical reasoning. In particular, the version of calculus that he published in 1684 established the notation and the rules for finding derivatives that we use today.

Unfortunately, a dreadful priority dispute arose in the 1690s between the followers of Newton and those of Leibniz as to who had invented calculus first. Leibniz was even accused of plagiarism by members of the Royal Society in England. The truth is that each man invented calculus independently. Newton arrived at his version of calculus first but, because of his fear of controversy, did not publish it immediately. So Leibniz’s 1684 account of calculus was the first to be published.
